summary:
Rio Grande do Norte stands under Brazil's national framework on legal gender recognition, anti-discrimination protection and the custody placement of LGBTI detainees. The sources reviewed record no state statute, state court ruling or state agency policy specific to Rio Grande do Norte on any of those questions, so the national assessment applies here unchanged.

Lethal violence against trans women is documented in the state across three consecutive reporting years. The ANTRA dossier for 2024, reported on 27 January 2025, records no trans or travesti killing in Rio Grande do Norte that year. The ninth ANTRA dossier, covering 2025, records four in the state, a figure tied with Paraíba and behind Ceará and Minas Gerais at eight each. Those state figures are drawn from a national total of 80 recorded killings in 2025 and are ranked by raw count alone; these sources give no per-capita denominator and no comparison with the state's general homicide rate, so the ranking does not measure per-head risk.

ANTRA states that official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly, so its counts are floors rather than complete totals. The sources also carry two irreconcilable figures for the state in 2025: the SBT News report of the ninth dossier lists four killings in Rio Grande do Norte, while a Saiba Mais article from February 2026 reproducing the same dossier records zero registered killings in the state for that year. The discrepancy is unresolved.

Naomi, a transgender woman, was found dead inside her own home in Praia da Pipa, in the Tibau do Sul municipality on the state's southern coast, in late February 2026, killed by stab wounds. The Civil Police opened an investigation and the Rio Grande do Norte trans-rights association ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN called for justice. No outcome of that investigation appears in these sources.

In the early hours of 4 May 2026 Emanuelle Samira Fernandes Neta, a 27-year-old transgender woman, was shot dead inside the rented house where she was sleeping on Rua Vivaldo Dantas in the Dom Jaime Câmara neighbourhood of Mossoró, in western Rio Grande do Norte, after five men broke in. Military police found the body on a routine patrol. One suspect was arrested carrying a pistol and booked for illegal firearms discharge and armed criminal association. ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN publicly mourned her as an artist killed by the transphobia she faced. This killing post-dates the state's recorded zero for 2024 and is the most recent documented instance in these sources.
tangentialFactors:
The state figures sit inside a national dataset whose totals move sharply year to year: 145 trans and travesti killings in 2023, 122 in 2024 (16% lower, close to the 125-per-year average for 2008–2024), and 80 in 2025, a 34% drop that still marks an 18th consecutive year at the top of the global tally. Rio Grande do Norte's move from zero recorded killings in 2024 to four in 2025 is described in the SBT News report as the sharpest deterioration in the dataset, but that description rests on raw counts with no population denominator.

Of the 122 killings recorded for 2024, 95.9% of the victims were travestis and trans women and five were human-rights defenders. Of the 80 recorded for 2025, 38 fell in the Northeast, the macroregion containing Rio Grande do Norte.

Two of the sources reviewed, the Wikipedia entries on LGBT rights in Brazil and on LGBTQ people in prison, address Brazil as a whole. The first states that transgender prisoners have a right to their social name, to be forwarded to women's prisons and to choose male or female clothing, footnoted to a piece archived in January 2012; the second, read on 28 September 2026, reports no trans-prisoner housing rule for Brazil or for Rio Grande do Norte. Neither carries a Rio Grande do Norte-specific rule.
localsOnly:
ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN operates in Rio Grande do Norte and is the association that publicly intervened in both 2026 killings documented here, naming the victims and demanding justice. It is the state-level point of reference visible in these sources.

No Rio Grande do Norte state prison placement policy for trans, travesti or intersex detainees appears in these sources; nothing in the inventory records how the state prison administration applies the national Council of Justice custody resolutions, and no state-level study comparable to the Rio de Janeiro prison census exists here.

ANTRA's finding that official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly bears directly on residents: the state's zero for 2024 in that count is a product of official recording practice, so a resident's killing may never enter the tally.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: the two figures for Rio Grande do Norte in 2025, four killings in one report of the ninth ANTRA dossier and zero in another reproduction of the same dossier, cannot be reconciled from these sources.

Not sourced: no per-capita figure, no population denominator and no general homicide rate for Rio Grande do Norte appear anywhere in the inventory, so the state's raw counts cannot be converted into a rate or compared with background violence.

Not sourced: the outcome of the Civil Police investigation into Naomi's killing, and whether the single arrest in the Mossoró case has progressed to prosecution. No later documented instance of lethal violence against a trans woman in the state appears in these sources beyond 4 May 2026.

Not sourced: any Rio Grande do Norte-specific signal on identity-document markers, entry screening, facilities access, hate-crime charging, or access to gender-affirming care. The inventory contains no state material on these questions, which is an absence of evidence rather than evidence of a settled position.
